## Timeout Distribution & Ramp Design

Measured from the live corpus (probe regen, `PRECOMPUTED.timeout_by_model`, 17 models): 0% ×2 (Opus 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite), 1.3–1.4% ×2, 4.3–6.4% ×4, 9.2–9.8% ×2, 13.7–15.0% ×3, 20.3–26.8% ×3, 45.8% ×1 (Gemma 4 31B). `rateStep`'s 50/90 breaks would dump 16/17 models into two steps.

**Chosen breaks:** 0 / >0 / ≥5% / ≥10% / ≥20% → spread **2/4/4/3/4**; round, readable thresholds (one-in-twenty / one-in-ten / one-in-five).

**Contrast (computed arithmetically, worse of #0a0f1c/#151d2e, 4.5:1 small-text floor):** fail-red is darker than pass-green, so the `rs-3`-style dark-text flip at α.65 **fails** on red (3.49:1) — `.to-3` instead keeps `--text-1` on a .55 fill (5.66:1). `.to-4` (.85) flips to `--surface-0` (5.24:1), with an `opacity:1` override on its `.lb-n` because the inherited .85 opacity measured 4.49:1 (a hair under floor). `.to-1` .16 (12.09:1) and `.to-2` .34 (8.62:1) mirror the rs-* alphas. All figures recorded in the CSS design comment.

## Learning Signal
**Learning Signal:** Process — Inverting a color ramp from a pass-hue to a fail-hue is not alpha-symmetric: the fail red (#f87171) is darker than the pass green (#34d399), so the dark-text flip threshold that passes WCAG on the green ramp (α.65) fails on red (3.49:1) — contrast must be recomputed per hue, never copied across families.
